673:.claude/rules/frontend.md:20:- **Editorial marketing layer**: the public marketing surface (unauthenticated `/`, `use-cases/*`, `compare/*`, `alternatives/*`, `features/*`, `tools/*`, `pricing`, `trust`, `demo`, `shared/[token]`, `document-diff`, `about`, `contact`, `imprint`, `privacy`, `terms`, `blog/*`) uses the scoped editorial system in `frontend/src/app/editorial.css` — every rule under `.dt-editorial`. **Light AND dark are both required** (HIG: every custom colour needs both): `.dt-editorial` is warm paper (`--ed-paper` `#eae8e3`, `--ed-ink` `#20211e`, `--ed-signal` terracotta `#843c28`), `.dark .dt-editorial` a warm near-black that is NOT an inversion and NOT zinc (`--ed-paper` `#171614`, `--ed-ink` `#ece9e2`, `--ed-signal` `#e0957a`). Olive = verified only; amber `--ed-evidence` = citation only. **Dark tokens must reuse the `--ed-*` names** — ~40 components write `var(--ed-paper-2)` inline and the `!important` counter-rule resolves `var(--ed-paper)`, so new names would leave them light-on-dark. Never hardcode `#fff`/`white` on an `--ed-*` background; use `var(--ed-paper)` so it inverts. Type: display steps (`.ed-display`, `.ed-h1`, `.ed-h2`, `.ed-num`, the header/footer wordmark) read `--ed-display-family` and never `var(--dt-serif)` directly — Fraunces 600 on paper (optical size follows the rendered size — do NOT pin `"opsz" 144`, it crowds words together at phone sizes), Geist on Night (below); Fraunces is declared with `preload: false` in `app/layout.tsx` — no page shows it at load since Night, the app's citation popover fetches it on first open, and preloading it cost every route 270 KB (tested); IBM Plex Sans for every other glyph; no italic `<em>` in headlines, no mono labels, no ALL-CAPS eyebrows. Structure follows Apple's grammar: one claim → one sentence → **exactly one filled `.ed-cta` per view** → the product; secondary actions use `.ed-cta-quiet` or `.ed-link`. Liquid Glass (`.ed-glass`) is permitted ONLY in the functional layer (the sticky header and popovers) — never on cards, FAQ rows, banners, tables or hero art. **Design decision 2026-09-20 (supersedes 2026-05-20):** the warm-paper terracotta identity is kept (re-affirmed by the owner, who chose it over a neutral rebrand), but the light-only rule, content-layer glass and 3px buttons are retired (its "app joins the paper system" clause, A2, was retired on 2026-09-21 — the app keeps zinc/blue). Do not re-propose a neutral/blue rebrand, and do not reintroduce a second surface treatment. Plan: `.collab/plans/2026-09-20-apple-design-direction.md`. **Night marketing surface (2026-09-21, owner decisions: prototype B for the landing, then "其他营销页也改成夜间"):** every marketing root — `LandingPageContent` and `MarketingShell`, the only two elements that open `.dt-editorial` — renders `NIGHT_ROOT_CLASS` from `components/marketing/night.ts` (`dt-editorial dt-night` + the Geist variable) and calls its `useNightDocument()` (reference-counted: theme-color swapped to the night stage and `dt-night-doc` on `<html>`, so overscroll and the scrollbar are dark too — the ONE editorial rule outside `.dt-editorial`, gated by that class): the editorial dark theme in BOTH OS themes — every `.dark .dt-editorial…` selector carries a `.dt-editorial.dt-night…` twin in the same selector list; never new token names. The owner then asked for prototype B's deeper ground and sans headline, so there is exactly ONE night-only value block (`.dt-editorial.dt-night`: stage `--ed-paper` `#0a0908`, `--ed-paper-2`, `--ed-glass`, `--ed-glass-strong`, `--ed-display-family` = Geist — a closed list) plus weight/tracking retunes for the display steps. Geist comes from the `geist` package and is imported by `night.ts` only, so app routes never preload it; the retunes sit BEFORE the non-Latin `:lang()` block so zh/ja/ko/hi/ar keep zero tracking (negative tracking breaks Arabic joining). `tests/landing-night.test.cjs` enforces the twin rule, the closed night-only list, both roots, the display-family indirection and Geist's single importer; a CDP contrast audit of 54 marketing pages (light OS) found zero text below AA at ship time. Chrome rendered outside the root mirrors the class (`CookieConsentBanner`, `EdLanguageSelector`'s portalled menu), and `LandingPageContent` tints `theme-color` while mounted. The hero is `CitationField` — a canvas whose colours come from the `--ed-*` tokens and whose font comes from the computed `--dt-body`, with no literals (tested); its rAF loop stops once the citation is marked, and reduced motion / `?still` draw the final frame — behind a real-text claim, with an opaque answer card under the passage and Quote Finder named in the footnote. The document text in `citationFieldContent.ts` is verbatim page 1 of a `backend/seed_data/` PDF (checked with `pdftotext`) and always renders `dir="ltr" lang="en"`; `landing.frame.{question,answer,source,description}` change together with it. The paper values stay the base of the token set, but no marketing page renders them now. The app keeps its zinc/blue palette (owner, 2026-09-21; A2 retired), so the step from a marketing page into the app is Night → app theme by design. Terracotta, Plex and the olive/amber roles are unchanged. Plan: `.collab/plans/2026-09-21-landing-night.md`. Marketing pages compose the shared editorial kit in `frontend/src/components/marketing/` (`MarketingShell`, `EditorialMarketingHeader`, `EdPageHero` — `variant="product"` for the product-first hero, `EdSection`, `EdProse`, `EdFeatureList`, `EdCardGrid`, `EdStepRow`, `EdFaqList`, `EdCtaBanner`, `EdComparisonTable`, `EdInlineCell`, `EdRelatedLinks`, `EdCheckList`, `EdChoiceList`) — `MarketingShell` supplies the `.dt-editorial` root, so kit components never add it themselves. Keep editorial styles scoped under `.dt-editorial`, including reduced-motion rules; do not let them leak into the functional app UI (`editorial.css` is imported globally, so an unscoped selector hits every app route). Do not apply the zinc/blue rule to editorial components. Two dual-surface components are sanctioned: `DocumentDiffPanel` takes `surface="app"|"editorial"`; the global `CookieConsentBanner` detects the surface itself (and mirrors Night). **Never touch one half of the `!important` pair alone**: `globals.css` `.dt-stitch-root > .min-h-screen { background: transparent !important }` and its `editorial.css` counter-rule `.dt-stitch-root > .dt-editorial` — removing either blanks the paper on every marketing page.

input for position t.This inherentlysequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longersequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples.Recent work has achievedsignificant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditionalcomputation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter.The fundamentalconstraint of sequential computation, however, remains.Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduction models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance inthe input or output sequences [2, 19].In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanismsare used in conjunction with a recurrent network.In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and insteadrelying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art intranslation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight sequence of symbol representations (x1, ..., xn) to a sequenceof continuous representations z = (z1, ..., zn).Given z, the decoder then generates an outputsequence (y1, ..., ym) of symbols one element Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fullyconnected layers for both the encoder and decoder, shown in the left and right halves of Figure 1,respectively.3.1Encoder and Decoder StacksThe encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.Each layer has twoEncoder:sub-layers.The first is a multi-head self-attention mechanism, and of each sub-layer isLayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)), where Sublayer(x) is the function implemented by the sub-layeritself.To facilitate these residual connections, all sub-layers in the model, as well as the embeddinglayers, produce outputs of dimension dmodel = 512.The decoder is also composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.In addition to the twoDecoder:sub-layers in each encoder layer, the decoder inserts a third sub-layer, which performs multi-headattention over the output of the encoder stack.Similar to the encoder, we employ residual connectionsaround each of the sub-layers, followed by layer normalization.We also modify the self-attentionsub-layer in the decoder stack to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions.Thismasking, combined with fact that the output established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling andtransduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [35, 2, 5].Numerousefforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoderarchitectures [38, 24, 15].Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and outputsequences.Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hiddenstates ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t.This inherentlysequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longersequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples.Recent work has achievedsignificant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditionalcomputation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter.The fundamentalconstraint of sequential computation, however, remains.Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduction models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance inthe input or output sequences [2, 19].In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanismsare used in conjunction with a recurrent network.In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and insteadrelying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art intranslation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.2BackgroundThe goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU[16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic buildingblock, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions.In these models,the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions growsin the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet.This makesit more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [12].In the Transformer this isreduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution dueto averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention asdescribed in section models are based on complex recurrent orconvolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder.The bestperforming models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attentionmechanism.We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer,based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutionsentirely.Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models tobe superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantlyless time to train.Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 Englishto-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, includingensembles, by over 2 BLEU.On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task,our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 aftertraining for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of thebest models from the literature.We show that the Transformer generalizes well toother tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both withlarge and limited training data.∗Equal contribution.Listing order is random.Jakob proposed replacing RNNs with self-attention and startedthe effort to evaluate this idea.Ashish, with Illia, designed and implemented the first Transformer models andhas been crucially involved in every aspect of this work.Noam proposed scaled dot-product attention, multi-headattention and the parameter-free position representation and became the other person involved in nearly everydetail.Niki designed, implemented, tuned and evaluated countless model variants in our original codebase andtensor2tensor.Llion also experimented with novel model variants, was responsible for our initial codebase, andefficient inference and Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA.1IntroductionRecurrent neural networks, long short-term memory [13] and gated recurrent [7] neural networksin particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling andtransduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [35, 2, 5].Numerousefforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoderarchitectures [38, 24, 15].Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and outputsequences.Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hiddenstates ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t.This inherentlysequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longersequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples.Recent work has achievedsignificant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditionalcomputation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter.The fundamentalconstraint of sequential computation, however, remains.Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduction models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance inthe input or output sequences [2, 19].In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanismsare used in conjunction with a recurrent network.In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and insteadrelying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art intranslation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.2BackgroundThe goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU[16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic buildingblock, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions.In these models,the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions growsin the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet.This makesit more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [12].In the Transformer this isreduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution dueto averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention asdescribed in section 3.2.Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positionsof a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence.Self-attention has beenused successfully in a variety of tasks including reading comprehension, abstractive summarization,", "page_start": 1, "page_end": 2, "section_title": memory [13] and gated recurrent [7] neural networksin particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling andtransduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [35, 2, 5].Numerousefforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoderarchitectures [38, 24, 15].Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and outputsequences.Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hiddenstates ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t.This inherentlysequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longersequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples.Recent work has achievedsignificant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditionalcomputation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter.The fundamentalconstraint of sequential computation, however, remains.Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduction models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance inthe input or output sequences [2, 19].In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanismsare used in conjunction with a recurrent network.In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and insteadrelying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art intranslation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.2BackgroundThe goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU[16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic buildingblock, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions.In these models,the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions growsin the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet.This makesit more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [12].In the Transformer this isreduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution dueto averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention asdescribed in section 3.2.Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positionsof a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence.Self-attention has beenused successfully in a variety of tasks including reading comprehension, abstractive summarization,", d2).Even with k = n, however, the complexity of a separableconvolution is equal to the combination of a self-attention layer and a point-wise feed-forward layer,the approach we take in our model.As Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA.1IntroductionRecurrent neural networks, long short-term memory [13] and gated recurrent [7] neural networksin particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling andtransduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [35, 2, 5].Numerousefforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoderarchitectures [38, 24, 15].Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and outputsequences.Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hiddenstates ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t.This inherentlysequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longersequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples.Recent work has achievedsignificant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditionalcomputation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter.The fundamentalconstraint of sequential computation, however, remains.Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduction models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance inthe input or output sequences [2, 19].In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanismsare used in conjunction with a recurrent network.In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and insteadrelying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art intranslation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.2BackgroundThe goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU[16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic buildingblock, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions.In these models,the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions growsin the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet.This makesit more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [12].In the Transformer this isreduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution dueto averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention asdescribed in section 3.2.Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positionsof a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence.Self-attention has beenused successfully in a variety of tasks including reading comprehension, abstractive summarization,", "page_start": 1, "page_end": 2, "section_title": structure [5, 2, 35].Here, the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations (x1, ..., xn) to a sequenceof continuous representations z = (z1, ..., zn).Given z, the decoder then generates an outputsequence (y1, ..., ym) of symbols one element at a time.At each step the model is auto-regressive[10], consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input when generating the next.2Figure 1: The Transformer - model architecture.The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fullyconnected layers for both the encoder and residual connections, all sub-layers in the model, as well as the embeddinglayers, produce outputs of dimension dmodel = 512.The decoder is also composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.In addition to the twoDecoder:sub-layers in each encoder layer, the decoder inserts a third sub-layer, which performs multi-headattention over the output of the encoder stack.Similar to the encoder, we employ residual connectionsaround each of the sub-layers, followed by layer normalization.We also modify the self-attentionsub-layer in the decoder stack to prevent positions from attending to width k < n does not connect all pairs of input and outputpositions.Doing so requires a stack of O(n/k) convolutional layers in the case of contiguous kernels,or O(logk(n)) in the case of dilated convolutions [18], increasing the length of the longest pathsbetween any two positions in the network.Convolutional layers are generally more expensive thanrecurrent layers, by a factor of k.Separable convolutions [6], however, decrease the complexityconsiderably, to O(k · n · d + n · d2).Even with k = n, however, the complexity of a separableconvolution is equal to the combination of a self-attention layer and a point-wise feed-forward layer,the approach we take in our model.As side benefit, self-attention could yield more interpretable models.We inspect attention distributionsfrom our models and present and discuss examples in the appendix.Not only do individual attentionheads clearly learn to perform different tasks, many appear to exhibit behavior related to the syntacticand "implementing tensor2tensor, replacing our earlier codebase, greatly improving results and massively acceleratingour research.†Work performed while at Google Brain.‡Work performed while at Google Research.31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA.1IntroductionRecurrent neural networks, long short-term memory [13] and gated recurrent [7] neural networksin particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling andtransduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [35, 2, 5].Numerousefforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoderarchitectures [38, 24, 15].Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and outputsequences.Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hiddenstates ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t.This inherentlysequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longersequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across residual connections, all sub-layers in the model, as well as the embeddinglayers, produce outputs of dimension dmodel = 512.The decoder is also composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.In addition to the twoDecoder:sub-layers in each encoder layer, the decoder inserts a third sub-layer, which performs multi-headattention over the output of the encoder stack.Similar to the encoder, we employ residual connectionsaround each of the sub-layers, followed by layer normalization.We also modify the self-attentionsub-layer in the decoder stack to prevent positions from attending to orconvolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder.The bestperforming models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attentionmechanism.We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer,based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutionsentirely.Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models tobe superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantlyless time to train.Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 Englishto-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, includingensembles, by over 2 BLEU.On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task,our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 aftertraining for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of thebest models from the literature.We show that the Transformer generalizes well toother tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both withlarge and limited training data.∗Equal contribution.Listing order is random.Jakob proposed replacing RNNs with self-attention and startedthe effort to evaluate this addition to the twoDecoder:sub-layers in each encoder layer, the decoder inserts a third sub-layer, which performs multi-headattention over the output of the encoder stack.Similar to the encoder, we Google Brain.‡Work performed while at Google Research.31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA.1IntroductionRecurrent neural networks, long short-term memory [13] and gated recurrent [7] neural networksin particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling andtransduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [35, 2, 5].Numerousefforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoderarchitectures [38, 24, 15].Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and outputsequences.Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hiddenstates ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t.This inherentlysequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longersequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples.Recent work has achievedsignificant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditionalcomputation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter.The fundamentalconstraint of sequential computation, however, remains.Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduction models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance inthe input or output sequences [2, 19].In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanismsare used in conjunction with a recurrent network.In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and insteadrelying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art intranslation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.2BackgroundThe goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU[16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic buildingblock, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions.In these models,the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions growsin the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet.This makesit more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [12].In the Transformer this isreduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution dueto averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention asdescribed in section 3.2.Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positionsof a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence.Self-attention has beenused successfully in a variety of tasks including reading comprehension, abstractive summarization,", centered around the respective output position.This would increase the maximumpath length to O(n/r).We plan to investigate this approach further in future work.A single convolutional layer with kernel width k < n does not connect all pairs of input and outputpositions.Doing so requires a stack of O(n/k) convolutional layers in the case of contiguous kernels,or O(logk(n)) in the case of dilated convolutions [18], increasing the length of the longest pathsbetween any two positions in the network.Convolutional layers are generally more expensive thanrecurrent layers, by a factor of k.Separable convolutions [6], however, decrease the complexityconsiderably, to O(k · n · d + n · d2).Even with k = n, however, the complexity of a separableconvolution is equal to the combination of a self-attention layer and a point-wise feed-forward layer,the approach we take in our model.As side benefit, self-attention could yield more interpretable models.We inspect attention distributionsfrom our models and present and discuss examples in the appendix.Not only do individual attentionheads clearly learn to perform different tasks, many appear to exhibit behavior related to the syntacticand results could differ materially from our estimates.On an on-going basis, we evaluate our estimates, includingthose related to revenue recognition, cash equivalents and marketable securities, accounts networksin particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling andtransduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [35, 2, 5].Numerousefforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoderarchitectures [38, 24, 15].Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and outputsequences.Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hiddenstates ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t.This inherentlysequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longersequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples.Recent work has achievedsignificant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditionalcomputation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter.The fundamentalconstraint of sequential computation, however, remains.Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduction models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance inthe input or output sequences [2, 19].In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanismsare used in conjunction with a recurrent network.In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and insteadrelying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art intranslation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.2BackgroundThe goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU[16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic buildingblock, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions.In these models,the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions growsin the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet.This makesit more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [12].In the Transformer this isreduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution dueto averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention asdescribed in section 3.2.Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positionsof a single sequence in order to compute a representation of ArchitectureMost competitive neural sequence transduction models have an encoder-decoder structure [5, 2, 35].Here, the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations (x1, ..., xn) to a sequenceof continuous representations z = (z1, ..., zn).Given z, the decoder then generates an outputsequence (y1, ..., ym) of symbols one element at a time.At each step the model is auto-regressive[10], consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input when generating the next.2Figure 1: The Transformer - model architecture.The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fullyconnected layers for both the encoder and decoder, shown in the left and right halves of Figure 1,respectively.3.1Encoder and Decoder StacksThe encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.Each layer has twoEncoder:sub-layers.The first is a multi-head self-attention mechanism, and the second is a simple, positionwise fully connected feed-forward network.We employ a residual connection [11] around each ofthe two sub-layers, followed by layer normalization [1].That is, the output of each sub-layer isLayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)), where Sublayer(x) is the function implemented by the sub-layeritself.To facilitate these residual connections, all sub-layers in the model, as well as the embeddinglayers, produce outputs of dimension dmodel = 512.The decoder is also composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.In addition to the twoDecoder:sub-layers in each encoder layer, the decoder inserts a third sub-layer, which performs multi-headattention over the output of the encoder stack.Similar to the encoder, we employ residual connectionsaround each of the sub-layers, followed by layer normalization.We also modify the self-attentionsub-layer in the decoder stack to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions.Thismasking, combined with fact that the output embeddings are networksin particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling andtransduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [35, 2, 5].Numerousefforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoderarchitectures [38, 24, 15].Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and outputsequences.Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hiddenstates ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t.This inherentlysequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longersequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples.Recent work has achievedsignificant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditionalcomputation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter.The fundamentalconstraint of sequential computation, however, remains.Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduction models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance inthe input or output sequences [2, 19].In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanismsare used in conjunction with a recurrent network.In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and insteadrelying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art intranslation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.2BackgroundThe goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU[16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic buildingblock, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions.In these models,the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions growsin the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet.This makesit more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [12].In the Transformer this isreduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution dueto averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention asdescribed in section 3.2.Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positionsof a single sequence in order to compute a representation of 4076:I did not run git. I did run `node --test frontend/tests/attribution.test.cjs`; it passes.
4078:1. **BLOCKER** — Raw `landing_path` can leak sensitive route tokens/IDs. [attribution.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:77) stores `url.pathname` verbatim, while auth can be opened from private document routes [DocumentReaderPageClient.tsx](</Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/d/[documentId]/DocumentReaderPageClient.tsx:307>) and shared links contain bearer-like tokens [shared page](</Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:48>). Fix: do not send raw paths. Whitelist public marketing slugs, and normalize/drop private or dynamic routes: `/d/[id]`, `/shared/[token]`, `/collections/[id]`, `/auth`, `/billing`, `/profile`, `/document-diff`.
4080:2. **BLOCKER** — “No identifiers” is not true for signed-in users. `trackEvent` posts to `/api/proxy/api/events` [analytics.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/analytics.ts:20); the proxy injects `Authorization` when an Auth.js token exists [route.ts](</Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts:107>); backend stores `user_id` on the event row [events.py](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/backend/app/api/events.py:120). Fix: either make these attribution events truly anonymous through a non-auth-injecting path, or change the privacy claim to “no analytics cookies or device identifiers; if you are signed in, product events may be associated with your account.”
4082:3. **SHOULD** — The privacy copy under-discloses what is collected. It says “sign-up or sign-in” and mentions domain/campaign tags only [en.json](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:220), but attribution is also attached to demo CTA clicks [HeroSection.tsx](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/components/landing/HeroSection.tsx:229) and includes `landing_path`. Fix: either stop adding attribution to demo CTAs, or disclose “key pre-signup buttons” plus sanitized landing page category/path. Also update the privacy “last updated” date from `2026-09-13` [PrivacyPageClient.tsx](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/privacy/PrivacyPageClient.tsx:27).
4084:4. **SHOULD** — UTM/referrer inputs are arbitrary strings, so campaign values can carry personal data. [attribution.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:74) accepts decoded `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, and `utm_campaign` after only trimming and length-capping. Fix: drop values containing emails, phone-ish strings, UUIDs/tokens, or path/query characters; keep `utm_source`/`utm_medium` tightly normalized, and treat `utm_campaign` as optional/lower-trust.
4086:5. **SHOULD** — Referrer filtering will create self-referrals and auth/return-hop noise. [referrerHost](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:55) only strips exact current host/`www` and three auth hosts. It does not ignore `*.doctalk.site`, Vercel preview deployments, `checkout.stripe.com`, common webmail magic-link referrers, non-HTTP schemes like `android-app://`, or Microsoft auth host variants. Fix: require `http:`/`https:` for `ref_host`, add robust own-host matching, and maintain a return-hop ignore list.
4088:6. **SHOULD** — Tests cover happy-path parsing, but not the risky paths. [attribution.test.cjs](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/tests/attribution.test.cjs:39) tests same-host and listed auth hosts, but not authenticated proxy association, dynamic route redaction, Vercel preview hosts, non-HTTP referrers, PII-ish UTM values, or module-cache first-touch after `window.location` changes. Add those before shipping.
4090:No SSR/hydration bug found: `window`/`document` reads are guarded, and App Router client navigation does not create a new `Document`, so `document.referrer` should remain the original document referrer rather than becoming the prior client-side route. References used: [MDN `document.referrer`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/referrer), [ePrivacy Directive Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/art_5/par_3/oj/eng), [GDPR Art. 4/5 text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32016R0679).
4092:Verdict: REWORK.

I did not run git. I did run `node --test frontend/tests/attribution.test.cjs`; it passes.

1. **BLOCKER** — Raw `landing_path` can leak sensitive route tokens/IDs. [attribution.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:77) stores `url.pathname` verbatim, while auth can be opened from private document routes [DocumentReaderPageClient.tsx](</Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/d/[documentId]/DocumentReaderPageClient.tsx:307>) and shared links contain bearer-like tokens [shared page](</Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:48>). Fix: do not send raw paths. Whitelist public marketing slugs, and normalize/drop private or dynamic routes: `/d/[id]`, `/shared/[token]`, `/collections/[id]`, `/auth`, `/billing`, `/profile`, `/document-diff`.

2. **BLOCKER** — “No identifiers” is not true for signed-in users. `trackEvent` posts to `/api/proxy/api/events` [analytics.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/analytics.ts:20); the proxy injects `Authorization` when an Auth.js token exists [route.ts](</Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts:107>); backend stores `user_id` on the event row [events.py](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/backend/app/api/events.py:120). Fix: either make these attribution events truly anonymous through a non-auth-injecting path, or change the privacy claim to “no analytics cookies or device identifiers; if you are signed in, product events may be associated with your account.”

3. **SHOULD** — The privacy copy under-discloses what is collected. It says “sign-up or sign-in” and mentions domain/campaign tags only [en.json](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:220), but attribution is also attached to demo CTA clicks [HeroSection.tsx](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/components/landing/HeroSection.tsx:229) and includes `landing_path`. Fix: either stop adding attribution to demo CTAs, or disclose “key pre-signup buttons” plus sanitized landing page category/path. Also update the privacy “last updated” date from `2026-09-13` [PrivacyPageClient.tsx](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/privacy/PrivacyPageClient.tsx:27).

4. **SHOULD** — UTM/referrer inputs are arbitrary strings, so campaign values can carry personal data. [attribution.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:74) accepts decoded `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, and `utm_campaign` after only trimming and length-capping. Fix: drop values containing emails, phone-ish strings, UUIDs/tokens, or path/query characters; keep `utm_source`/`utm_medium` tightly normalized, and treat `utm_campaign` as optional/lower-trust.

5. **SHOULD** — Referrer filtering will create self-referrals and auth/return-hop noise. [referrerHost](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:55) only strips exact current host/`www` and three auth hosts. It does not ignore `*.doctalk.site`, Vercel preview deployments, `checkout.stripe.com`, common webmail magic-link referrers, non-HTTP schemes like `android-app://`, or Microsoft auth host variants. Fix: require `http:`/`https:` for `ref_host`, add robust own-host matching, and maintain a return-hop ignore list.

6. **SHOULD** — Tests cover happy-path parsing, but not the risky paths. [attribution.test.cjs](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/tests/attribution.test.cjs:39) tests same-host and listed auth hosts, but not authenticated proxy association, dynamic route redaction, Vercel preview hosts, non-HTTP referrers, PII-ish UTM values, or module-cache first-touch after `window.location` changes. Add those before shipping.

No SSR/hydration bug found: `window`/`document` reads are guarded, and App Router client navigation does not create a new `Document`, so `document.referrer` should remain the original document referrer rather than becoming the prior client-side route. References used: [MDN `document.referrer`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/referrer), [ePrivacy Directive Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/art_5/par_3/oj/eng), [GDPR Art. 4/5 text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32016R0679).

Verdict: REWORK.

    81	    if value is None:

    83	    text = str(value).strip()

    89	def _safe_properties(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:

    91	    for key, value in list(raw.items())[:20]:
    92	        safe_key = _safe_text(key, 64)
    93	        if not safe_key:
    94	            continue
    95	        if isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None:
    96	            safe[safe_key] = value if not isinstance(value, str) else value[:256]
    97	        else:
    98	            safe[safe_key] = str(value)[:256]

frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:245:  "privacy.ccpa.content": "نحن لا نبيع المعلومات الشخصية. يمكن لسكان كاليفورنيا التواصل عبر privacy@doctalk.site لطلب الوصول أو الحذف أو التصحيح أو معلومات إلغاء الاشتراك.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:248:  "privacy.section1.content": "نجمع عنوان بريدك الإلكتروني للمصادقة والمستندات التي ترفعها للتحليل. عند استخدام الأزرار الرئيسية قبل التسجيل (مثل التسجيل أو تسجيل الدخول أو تجربة العرض التوضيحي)، نسجّل أيضًا نطاق الموقع الذي أحالك إلينا ووسوم الحملة الموجودة في الرابط (مثل utm_source) ونوع الصفحة التي وصلت إليها، لنعرف كيف يصل الناس إلى DocTalk. لا يُنشئ ذلك ملفات تعريف ارتباط ولا أي معرّف للجهاز؛ وإذا كنت مسجّل الدخول، تُربط هذه الأحداث بحسابك مثل أحداث المنتج الأخرى لدينا.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:249:  "privacy.section1.title": "جمع البيانات",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:250:  "privacy.section2.item1": "لا تدرب DocTalk النماذج على بياناتك",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:251:  "privacy.section2.item2": "تُعالج المستندات لتوفير ميزات المستندات التي تطلبها.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:252:  "privacy.section2.item3": "بحسب الميزة والإعدادات، قد تعالج DeepSeek المحتوى والأسئلة ذات الصلة مباشرةً، أو تتم معالجتها عبر OpenRouter ومزوديها، أو لدى مزودي OCR والترجمة. لا تبيع DocTalk بياناتك ولا تستخدمها لتدريب النماذج. تختلف شروط الاحتفاظ والتدريب باختلاف الخدمة والإعدادات؛ ولا يوجد ضمان شامل بعدم الاحتفاظ بالبيانات.",

frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:254:  "privacy.section3.content": "المستندات مشفرة أثناء التخزين باستخدام AES-256. يمكنك حذف بياناتك في أي وقت من إعدادات حسابك.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:255:  "privacy.section3.title": "تخزين البيانات",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:256:  "privacy.section4.content": "يمكنك حذف مستندات منفردة، أو تصدير بيانات الحساب وحذف حسابك من الملف الشخصي ← الحساب. لطلبات الخصوصية الأخرى، تواصل مع privacy@doctalk.site.",

frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:783:  "about.description": "يساعد DocTalk الأشخاص على قراءة المستندات المكثفة بشكل أسرع دون التخلي عن إمكانية التتبع. قم بتحميل ملف PDF أو DOCX أو PPTX أو XLSX أو TXT أو Markdown أو رابط عام، واطرح أسئلة باللغة الطبيعية، وارجع إلى المقطع المصدر المُستشهد به بنقرة واحدة.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:784:  "about.optimizeFor.title": "ما نحسّن من أجله",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:785:  "about.optimizeFor.item1": "إجابات قابلة للتحقق مع استشهادات تشير إلى النص المصدر الأصلي.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:786:  "about.optimizeFor.item2": "دعم سير عمل المستندات الحقيقية، وليس فقط PDF.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:787:  "about.optimizeFor.item3": "انضمام سريع، بما في ذلك عرض توضيحي عام يعمل قبل التسجيل.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:788:  "about.optimizeFor.item4": "معالجة تركز على الخصوصية للملفات المرفوعة وبيانات الحساب.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:789:  "about.whoUses.title": "من يستخدم DocTalk",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:790:  "about.whoUses.item1": "الطلاب والباحثون الذين يراجعون الأوراق والمصادر التقنية.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:791:  "about.whoUses.item2": "فرق القانونية والمالية والموارد البشرية التي تعمل على مستندات طويلة ومليئة بالتفاصيل.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:792:  "about.whoUses.item3": "المشغلون والمؤسسون الذين يحتاجون إجابات سريعة من العقود والعروض التقديمية والتقارير.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:793:  "about.whoUses.item4": "أي شخص يريد مساعدة الذكاء الاصطناعي دون فقدان القدرة على التحقق من المصدر.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:794:  "about.trust.title": "الثقة والخصوصية واتجاه المنتج",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:795:  "about.trust.paragraph1": "تم بناء DocTalk حول التوليد المعزز بالاسترجاع بحيث تظل الإجابات قائمة على المستند الذي تم تحميله. يدعم المنتج تمييز الاستشهادات وأوضاع أداء متعددة وسير عمل المستندات عبر عدة تنسيقات. يتم تشفير المستندات المرفوعة أثناء النقل وفي وضع السكون، ويمكن للمستخدمين إدارة بياناتهم أو حذفها من التطبيق.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:796:  "about.trust.paragraph2": "يركز المنتج العام الحالي على صفحات تحسين محركات البحث باللغة الإنجليزية، بينما تدعم واجهة التطبيق 11 لغة. يتم نشر تحديثات المنتج والمقارنات والأدلة العملية على المدونة مع تطور المنتج.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:797:  "about.howItWorks.title": "كيف يعمل المنتج",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:798:  "about.howItWorks.description": "خلف الواجهة، يجمع DocTalk بين تحليل المستندات وتقسيمها واسترجاعها وتوليد نموذج اللغة بحيث تظل الإجابات مرتبطة بالملف الأصلي. هذه البنية مهمة لأن المنتج لا يحاول استبدال المستند المصدر. إنه يحاول تقصير المسار من السؤال إلى الأدلة القابلة للتحقق داخل المستند الذي لديك بالفعل.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:799:  "about.whatWePublish.title": "ما ننشره",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:800:  "about.whatWePublish.description": "تركز الصفحات العامة على DocTalk على تعليم المنتج العملي: شروحات الميزات وحالات الاستخدام ومقارنات البرامج ومنشورات المدونة حول سير عمل مستندات الذكاء الاصطناعي. الهدف واضح: مساعدة المستخدمين على فهم أين تكمن قوة المنتج، وأين تهم الاستشهادات، وأي سير عمل تناسب الأداة فعليًا قبل التسجيل.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:801:  "about.contact.title": "اتصل بنا",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:802:  "about.contact.description1": "يمكن إرسال الأسئلة حول المنتج أو الشراكات أو الخصوصية أو الدعم إلى",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:803:  "about.contact.description2": ". يمكنك أيضًا العثور على قاعدة الشيفرة البرمجية العامة على",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:807:  "contact.description": "أسرع طريقة للتواصل هي البريد الإلكتروني. نستخدم صندوق وارد واحد للدعم والخصوصية وملاحظات المنتج حتى لا تضيع الطلبات عبر القنوات المختلفة.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:808:  "contact.primary.title": "جهة الاتصال الرئيسية",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:809:  "contact.primary.emailLabel": "البريد الإلكتروني:",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:810:  "contact.primary.useFor": "استخدم هذا العنوان لدعم الحساب ومشكلات الفوترة وطلبات الخصوصية واستفسارات الشراكات وتقارير الأخطاء وملاحظات المنتج العامة.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:811:  "contact.primary.usefulMessages": "تتضمن الرسائل المفيدة نوع المستند المعني والمسار أو الشاشة التي كنت عليها بالضبط والطوابع الزمنية ولقطات الشاشة وعنوان البريد الإلكتروني المرتبط بحساب DocTalk الخاص بك. وهذا يجعل الدعم أسهل بكثير لإعادة الإنتاج والحل دون تبادل طويل للرسائل.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:812:  "contact.support.title": "الدعم والفوترة",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:813:  "contact.support.description": "قم بتضمين البريد الإلكتروني المرتبط بحساب DocTalk الخاص بك ووصفًا موجزًا للمشكلة وأي لقطات شاشة أو رسائل خطأ ذات صلة لتسريع الحل.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:814:  "contact.privacy.title": "الخصوصية والبيانات",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/ar.json:815:  "contact.privacy.description": "يمكن إرسال الأسئلة حول البيانات المصدرة أو طلبات الحذف أو توقعات الخصوصية إلى صندوق وارد الدعم نفسه للمتابعة.",
