frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:793:  "about.optimizeFor.item4": "Privacy-first handling for uploaded files and account data.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:799:  "about.trust.title": "Trust, privacy, and product direction",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:800:  "about.trust.paragraph1": "DocTalk is built around retrieval-augmented generation so answers stay grounded in the uploaded document. The product supports citation highlighting, multiple performance modes, and document workflows across several formats. Uploaded documents are encrypted in transit and at rest, and users can manage or delete their data from the app.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:801:  "about.trust.paragraph2": "The current public product focuses on English SEO pages, while the application interface supports 11 languages. Product updates, comparisons, and practical guides are published on the blog as the product evolves.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:802:  "about.howItWorks.title": "How the product works",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:803:  "about.howItWorks.description": "Behind the interface, DocTalk combines document parsing, chunking, retrieval, and language model generation so answers stay connected to the original file. That architecture matters because the product is not trying to replace the source document. It is trying to shorten the path from question to verifiable evidence inside the document you already have.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:805:  "about.whatWePublish.description": "Public pages on DocTalk focus on practical product education: feature explainers, use cases, software comparisons, and blog posts about AI document workflows. The goal is straightforward: help users understand where the product is strong, where citations matter, and which workflow the tool is actually suited for before they sign up.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:807:  "about.contact.description1": "Questions about the product, partnerships, privacy, or support can be sent to",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:809:  "about.contact.evaluationHint": "If you are evaluating DocTalk for a real workflow, the fastest way to build context is to start with the public demo, then review the pricing and feature pages. Those pages show the current product surface more accurately than generic AI-tool directories.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:812:  "contact.description": "The fastest way to get in touch is email. We use one inbox for support, privacy, and product feedback so requests do not get lost across channels.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:815:  "contact.primary.useFor": "Use this address for account support, billing issues, privacy requests, partnership inquiries, bug reports, and general product feedback.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:816:  "contact.primary.usefulMessages": "Useful messages include the document type involved, the exact route or screen you were on, timestamps, screenshots, and the email address associated with your DocTalk account. That makes support much easier to reproduce and resolve without a long back-and-forth.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:818:  "contact.support.description": "Include the email on your DocTalk account, a short description of the issue, and any relevant screenshots or error messages to speed up resolution.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:826:  "contact.when.goodReasons.item4": "Partnerships, integrations, or product feedback",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:830:  "contact.when.beforeYouSend.item3": "Tell us whether the issue is billing, product, or privacy related",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:831:  "contact.when.beforeYouSend.item4": "Use the account email if the request involves account access",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:838:  "useCasesHub.cases.students.description": "Analyze research papers, textbooks, and dissertations with AI. Get cited answers with page-level references to speed up literature reviews and exam prep.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:856:  "useCasesHub.crossLinks.description": "Use cases land better when readers can immediately see which feature or comparison page answers the next question.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:873:  "useCasesFinance.challenge.p1": "Financial analysis demands extracting precise data from dense, lengthy documents. A typical 10-K filing from a large public company runs 100 to 300 pages, packed with financial statements, footnotes, risk factor disclosures, management discussion and analysis (MD&A), and legal boilerplate. Quarterly 10-Q filings add another layer of data points every three months. Analysts covering multiple companies may need to review thousands of pages each earnings season.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:874:  "useCasesFinance.challenge.p2": "The critical information is often buried deep. Revenue recognition policy changes might be disclosed in footnote 14 on page 87. A material litigation risk might appear in a single paragraph of the risk factors section. A change in accounting estimates could be mentioned in the MD&A section with an impact quantified only in a supplemental table. Missing these details can mean missing a material investment risk.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:875:  "useCasesFinance.challenge.p3": "Earnings call transcripts present a different challenge. They are conversational in format, often 30 to 50 pages of dialogue between executives and analysts. Finding the specific comment where the CFO discussed margin expectations, or where the CEO addressed a competitive threat, requires reading or searching through the entire transcript.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:891:  "useCasesFinance.docTypes.pdf10K.detail": "SEC annual and quarterly reports from EDGAR or company investor relations pages. Handles complex multi-column layouts, financial tables, and footnotes.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:900:  "useCasesFinance.realWorld.annualReport.p1": "An equity analyst covering a technology company uploads the 200-page 10-K filing and asks: \"What was the total revenue and year-over-year growth rate?\" DocTalk returns the figures with a citation pointing to the consolidated statements of operations on page 54. A follow-up question, \"What are the main risk factors related to competition?\" surfaces three specific risk factor paragraphs from pages 18 through 22, each with its own citation.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:904:  "useCasesFinance.realWorld.earningsCall.p2": "This workflow is especially valuable during earnings season when analysts need to process multiple transcripts in a single day. Instead of reading each 40-page transcript end to end, they can ask the same set of targeted questions across multiple company calls and compare the responses.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:906:  "useCasesFinance.realWorld.quarterlyComparison.p1": "A portfolio manager uploads a company's Q2 and Q3 10-Q filings in separate sessions. For each, they ask the same set of questions: \"What was the gross margin?\" \"What were the operating expenses by category?\" \"Were there any impairment charges?\" The cited answers from each quarter are compiled into a comparison, with every data point traceable to the specific filing and page. This structured approach to quarterly tracking ensures nothing is missed and every figure is verifiable.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:912:  "useCasesFinance.whyCitations.p1": "Financial analysis lives and dies by accuracy. A revenue figure off by a few percentage points changes a valuation model. A missed footnote about an accounting policy change can invalidate an entire analysis. In this context, an AI tool that generates answers without verifiable sources is a liability, not an asset.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:935:  "useCasesFinance.cta.description": "Try DocTalk's free demo with sample documents. See how AI-powered citation highlighting works on real reports. No account required.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:947:  "useCasesLawyers.challenge.p1": "Legal work is, at its core, document work. A single corporate transaction can involve hundreds of contracts, disclosures, and regulatory filings. A litigation matter may require reviewing thousands of pages of court records, depositions, and correspondence. The volume is staggering, and the stakes of missing a critical clause are enormous.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:949:  "useCasesLawyers.challenge.p3": "Contract review is equally demanding. A 60-page commercial lease contains dozens of interdependent provisions. Termination clauses reference indemnification sections, which in turn reference insurance requirements. Understanding the full picture requires cross-referencing multiple sections, a task that is time-consuming even for experienced attorneys.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:953:  "useCasesLawyers.features.clauseExtraction.description": "Ask \"Find all indemnification clauses\" or \"Where are the termination provisions?\" DocTalk scans the entire document and returns every relevant clause with numbered citations pointing to the exact section and page.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:967:  "useCasesLawyers.docTypes.pdfContracts.detail": "Commercial leases, service agreements, NDAs, employment contracts, licensing agreements, and any other contract type. Handles multi-page documents with complex formatting.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:976:  "useCasesLawyers.realWorld.contractReview.p1": "An associate reviewing a 45-page commercial lease uploads the PDF to DocTalk and asks: \"Find all indemnification clauses.\" DocTalk returns three results, each with a numbered citation pointing to the exact section. Citation [1] links to Section 14.2, a broad mutual indemnification provision. Citation [2] links to Section 14.3, a carve-out for environmental liability. Citation [3] links to Exhibit B, an additional indemnification related to pre-existing conditions.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:977:  "useCasesLawyers.realWorld.contractReview.p2": "The associate then asks: \"What are the termination conditions?\" and \"Is there a cap on liability?\" Each answer references specific clauses with page numbers, allowing the associate to build a clause summary in minutes rather than hours. The citations make it easy to verify the AI's extraction against the actual contract language.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:982:  "useCasesLawyers.realWorld.courtFiling.p1": "A litigator receives opposing counsel's 30-page motion for summary judgment and needs to understand the key arguments quickly. They upload the filing and ask: \"Summarize the main arguments for summary judgment.\" DocTalk returns a structured summary, with each argument cited to specific paragraphs in the motion.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:983:  "useCasesLawyers.realWorld.courtFiling.p2": "Follow-up questions refine the analysis: \"What cases does the motion cite for the standard of review?\" surfaces the precedent citations. \"What facts does opposing counsel rely on for the absence of genuine dispute?\" pinpoints the factual arguments. Each answer points to the specific page, allowing the litigator to read the original language in context before drafting a response.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1003:  "useCasesLawyers.security.items.dataExport.detail": "Export all your data at any time through the account settings. Full GDPR Article 20 data portability support.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1019:  "useCasesLawyers.faq.q4.answer": "DocTalk works best with text-based PDFs where the text layer is preserved. For scanned or image-only PDFs, DocTalk automatically runs OCR using Tesseract (English + Simplified Chinese) to extract text. OCR quality varies with scan resolution and page layout — for legal work requiring high fidelity, text-based PDFs remain the most reliable source.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1023:  "useCasesLawyers.cta.description": "Try DocTalk's free demo with sample documents. See how AI-powered citation highlighting works on real documents. No account required.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1048:  "featuresMultilingual.howItWorks.p3": "The entire DocTalk interface — buttons, menus, labels, error messages, billing pages — is fully localized in all 11 languages. Switch languages anytime using the language selector in the header, and the entire application updates instantly.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1078:  "featuresMultilingual.cjk.p3": "Citation highlighting works with CJK text the same way as Latin text — click a citation to jump to the source passage and see it highlighted on the page. The semantic search engine indexes CJK text natively, so questions about Chinese, Japanese, or Korean documents return accurate, relevant passages.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1121:  "featuresPerformance.mode.thorough.description": "Legacy mode retained only for historical usage records.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1122:  "featuresPerformance.mode.thorough.bestFor1": "Historical usage records",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1138:  "featuresPerformance.faq.a3": "Yes, with a monthly cap. Free accounts can use Flash mode plus up to 20 Pro answers per month with 300 credits per month. Plus and Pro remove the Pro-mode monthly cap.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1142:  "featuresPerformance.cta.subtitle": "The free demo uses Flash mode. Sign up free for Flash and up to 20 Pro answers per month, or upgrade to Plus for unrestricted Pro usage.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1151:  "featuresDemo.hero.subtitle": "Chat with AI about sample documents instantly. No account, no credit card, no email. See citation highlighting, multi-format support, and performance modes in action with 3 demo documents ready to explore.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1152:  "featuresDemo.metaDescription": "Chat with AI about sample documents instantly. No account, no credit card, no email. See citation highlighting, multi-format support, and performance modes in action with 3 demo documents ready to explore.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1157:  "featuresDemo.docs.doc1.description": "A real PDF document ready for AI analysis. Ask questions and see citation highlighting with page-level navigation.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1172:  "featuresDemo.compare.subtitle": "The demo is a preview. Free accounts unlock your own uploads. Paid plans unlock more credits and features.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1190:  "featuresDemo.steps.step1.description": "Go to the demo page — no account, no email, nothing to fill in.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1199:  "featuresDemo.faq.a1": "Yes. The demo is completely free. No credit card, no account, no email. Just click and start chatting with AI about the sample documents. If you want to upload your own documents, the free plan gives you 300 credits per month — also with no credit card required.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1200:  "featuresDemo.faq.q2": "Do I need an account?",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1201:  "featuresDemo.faq.a2": "Not for the demo. The demo works instantly without any registration. To upload your own documents and save your chat history, you will need a free account, which you can create with Google, Microsoft, or email.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1203:  "featuresDemo.faq.a3": "Nothing happens automatically. You can use the demo as many times as you want. When you are ready to upload your own documents, create a free account (300 credits/month) or upgrade to Plus ($9.99/month, 3,000 credits) or Pro ($19.99/month, 9,000 credits).",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1205:  "featuresDemo.faq.a4": "Yes. Create a free account (no credit card needed) and you can upload up to 3 documents (50MB each) with 300 credits per month. That is enough for dozens of questions using Flash mode.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1207:  "featuresDemo.faq.a5": "The demo does not use credits. Once you have an account, the free plan includes 300 credits per month. Flash is optimized for lower-cost questions, and Pro uses more credits for deeper analysis. Plus ($9.99) gives you 3,000 credits and Pro ($19.99) gives you 9,000.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1226:  "featuresHub.layoutTranslationDesc": "Translate text-heavy PDFs into a new PDF while preserving page structure, citations, equations, and visual context. Free includes 2 trials; Plus unlocks ongoing use.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1232:  "featuresHub.workflowsDesc": "DocTalk works best when you connect product capabilities to an actual job: research, legal review, finance analysis, or tool evaluation.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1238:  "featuresHub.ctaText": "See it all in action with the free demo — no account required.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1243:  "featuresLayoutTranslation.heroSubtitle": "Turn text-heavy PDFs into translated PDFs while keeping page structure, equations, citations, and visual context.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1244:  "featuresLayoutTranslation.metaDescription": "Turn text-heavy PDFs into translated PDFs while keeping page structure, equations, citations, and visual context.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1252:  "featuresLayoutTranslation.trialBody": "Every free account includes 2 layout-preserving PDF translations. After that, the workflow becomes a Plus and Pro feature, which makes it a concrete upgrade reason for users who work with foreign-language papers, contracts, manuals, and reports.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1265:  "featuresCitations.howStep1Desc": "Type any question in the chat panel. DocTalk uses semantic search (RAG) to find the most relevant passages from your entire document, whether it is 5 pages or 500.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1276:  "featuresCitations.layersSubtitle": "DocTalk does not just append page numbers. It builds citations from three independent layers of document understanding.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1280:  "featuresCitations.layer2Desc": "Each retrieved passage carries metadata about its location: the page number, section heading, and position in the document. When the AI generates a citation, it attaches this location data so you know exactly where in the document the information came from.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1282:  "featuresCitations.layer3Desc": "The final layer is the interactive highlight experience. Click any citation and the document viewer scrolls to the source passage. For PDFs, this uses bounding box coordinates to highlight the exact text region on the page. For DOCX, PPTX, and other text-based formats, it uses progressive text-snippet matching to locate and highlight the passage.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1312:  "featuresCitations.faq2A": "Yes. Every numbered citation in an AI answer is clickable. Clicking it scrolls the document viewer to the exact source passage and highlights it in yellow so you can read the original text in context. For PDFs, this highlights the bounding box region on the page. For other formats, it uses text-snippet matching.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1315:  "featuresCitations.faq4Q": "How does DocTalk prevent hallucination?",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1318:  "featuresCitations.faq5A": "Yes. Citation highlighting is available on all plans, including the free tier with 300 credits per month. You can also try it instantly in the free demo without creating an account.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1320:  "featuresCitations.ctaSubtitle": "Try the free demo to experience citation highlighting yourself. Upload a document or chat with one of our sample files. No account required.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1337:  "featuresMultiFormat.formatPdfDesc": "Full text extraction with page-level citations and bounding box highlighting. Supports scanned documents, complex layouts, and CJK characters.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1351:  "featuresMultiFormat.formatUrlExt": "Any web page",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1352:  "featuresMultiFormat.formatUrlDesc": "Web page content extraction and analysis. Paste any URL and chat with the page content using the same citation and highlighting features.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1366:  "featuresMultiFormat.detailPdfText": "Bounding box citation highlighting pinpoints the exact text region on each page. Full CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) character support with proper CMap rendering.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1376:  "featuresMultiFormat.detailUrlText": "Web page content is extracted and cleaned, removing navigation, ads, and boilerplate. The article content is then available for AI chat with the same citation features.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1399:  "featuresMultiFormat.faq4Q": "Can I chat with a webpage?",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1400:  "featuresMultiFormat.faq4A": "Yes. Paste any URL and DocTalk extracts the web page content automatically. The extracted text is then available for AI chat with the same citation highlighting feature as any uploaded document.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1402:  "featuresMultiFormat.faq5A": "Direct uploads use plan limits: Free supports 50 MB and 750 pages, Plus supports 100 MB and 1,500 pages, and Pro supports 200 MB and 3,000 pages. URL imports are capped at 10 MB on every plan.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1420:  "compareHub.widenTitle": "Widen the research path",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1421:  "compareHub.widenDescription": "Head-to-head pages convert best when readers can branch into category guides, alternatives, and the core features behind the verdict.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1460:  "compareChatpdf.whatIsDocTalkDescription": "DocTalk is an AI-powered document question-and-answer platform that supports seven file formats: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, TXT, Markdown, and web URLs. Upload any document, ask questions in natural language, and receive answers with real-time citation highlighting that scrolls to and visually highlights the exact source passage in your original document. The interface supports 11 languages, offers two AI performance modes (Flash and Pro), and includes a free demo that requires no account creation. DocTalk is designed for students, researchers, legal professionals, and anyone who needs to extract information from documents quickly while maintaining full traceability to the source material.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1462:  "compareChatpdf.whatIsChatPDFDescription": "ChatPDF is one of the earliest AI PDF chat tools, launched in early 2023. It allows users to upload PDF files and ask questions about their contents using a conversational interface. The tool references page numbers in its answers, making it possible to locate information manually. ChatPDF has built a large user base thanks to its simplicity and early-mover advantage. The free tier allows 2 PDFs per day with 3 questions each, while the Plus plan ($19.99/month) removes these limits. ChatPDF focuses solely on PDF files and does not support other document formats like Word, PowerPoint, or Excel.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1465:  "compareChatpdf.feature.formatSupportP1": "This is the most significant difference between the two tools. ChatPDF supports only PDF files. If you need to analyze a Word document, a PowerPoint presentation, an Excel spreadsheet, or a web page, you must first convert it to PDF before uploading, which is inconvenient and can introduce formatting issues.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1468:  "compareChatpdf.feature.formatSupportP2Post": " page for details.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1470:  "compareChatpdf.feature.citationsP1": "Both tools use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to answer questions based on your document content. ChatPDF provides page number references in its responses, which helps you know roughly where to look. However, you need to manually scroll to the referenced page and search for the relevant passage yourself.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1475:  "compareChatpdf.feature.languagesP2Pre": "DocTalk provides a fully localized interface in 11 languages: English, Chinese, Spanish, Japanese, German, French, Korean, Portuguese, Italian, Arabic, and Hindi. Every element of the interface, from buttons and labels to error messages and billing pages, is translated. The AI can also respond in the same language as your question, regardless of the document language. This makes DocTalk a strong choice for multilingual teams and non-English speakers. See our ",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1477:  "compareChatpdf.feature.languagesP2Post": " page.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1482:  "compareChatpdf.feature.pricingP2Mid": " that requires absolutely no signup, so you can try the product before creating an account. The free tier includes 300 credits per month. The Plus plan ($9.99/month) includes 3,000 credits, unrestricted Pro mode, and export features. The Pro plan ($19.99/month) adds 9,000 credits and custom instructions. DocTalk is generally more affordable: the Plus plan at $9.99 offers comparable or better value than ChatPDF Plus at $19.99. View ",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1489:  "compareChatpdf.feature.securityP2": "DocTalk implements AES-256 encryption for all uploaded documents, SSRF protection for URL ingestion, magic-byte file validation to prevent malicious uploads, and structured security event logging. Documents are never used to train AI models. DocTalk also provides a GDPR data export endpoint and cookie consent management. The OAuth implementation strips tokens after linking, and the Docker deployment runs as a non-root user for defense in depth.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1511:  "compareChatpdf.faq.a2": "ChatPDF mentions page numbers in its answers but does not offer inline citation highlighting. DocTalk provides real-time citation highlighting that visually highlights the exact passage in your document when you click a citation, making it much easier to verify AI answers.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1513:  "compareChatpdf.faq.a3": "Yes. DocTalk offers an instant demo that requires no signup at all, plus a free tier with 300 credits per month after you create an account. ChatPDF offers a free tier limited to 2 PDFs per day with 3 questions each.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1526:  "compareChatpdf.ctaDescription": "Upload a document and see citation highlighting in action. No account needed.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1552:  "compareNotebooklm.table.competitor.freeTier": "Free (Google account required)",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1562:  "compareNotebooklm.whatIsNotebookLMDescription": "Google NotebookLM (formerly Project Tailwind) is a free AI-powered research tool that lets you create notebooks with multiple source documents. You can upload PDFs, link Google Docs, paste text, and add web URLs or YouTube videos as sources. The AI synthesizes information across all sources in a notebook, making it useful for literature reviews and research projects. NotebookLM is unique in offering AI-generated audio podcasts that summarize your sources as a natural-sounding conversation. It runs on Google Gemini and is deeply integrated with the Google ecosystem. A Google account is required.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1577:  "compareNotebooklm.feature.pricingP1": "NotebookLM is currently free. This is its biggest advantage. Google has not disclosed future pricing, but as with many Google products, it may remain free with usage limits while offering premium features at a cost. The tradeoff is that you are building your workflow inside Google ecosystem.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1603:  "compareNotebooklm.verdictP3Pre": "If you primarily need multi-source synthesis and love Google products, NotebookLM is excellent. If you need precise citation verification, work with business document formats, or want to avoid Google dependency, ",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1610:  "compareNotebooklm.faq.a2": "Yes, Google NotebookLM is currently free to use, though it requires a Google account. Google has not yet announced pricing for future premium features. However, being free means you are subject to Google data practices and potential changes in service terms.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1613:  "compareNotebooklm.faq.q4": "Can I use DocTalk without a Google account?",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1614:  "compareNotebooklm.faq.a4": "Yes. DocTalk supports Google OAuth, Microsoft OAuth, and email magic links for authentication. You can also use the instant demo with no account at all. NotebookLM requires a Google account, which may be a concern for users who prefer not to use Google services.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1616:  "compareNotebooklm.faq.a5": "DocTalk stores documents with AES-256 encryption, never trains AI on your data, and provides GDPR data export. NotebookLM is a Google product subject to Google privacy policies. DocTalk gives you more control and transparency over your data.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1624:  "compareNotebooklm.ctaDescription": "No Google account needed. Upload a document and experience citation highlighting instantly.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1637:  "altsHub.decisionTitle": "Move from list posts to decision pages",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1638:  "altsHub.decisionDescription": "Alternative roundups are stronger when readers can jump straight into a verdict, a pricing page, or the feature that matters most to them.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1667:  "altsChatpdf.alt1Desc2": "The standout feature is real-time citation highlighting. When the AI answers your question, every citation is a clickable link. Click it and the document viewer scrolls to the exact passage with a visual highlight overlay. This is a fundamental improvement over ChatPDF page number references, which require you to manually find the relevant text. For academic papers, legal documents, or any research where accuracy matters, this one feature alone justifies switching.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1685:  "altsChatpdf.alt3Desc2": "For individual users, Humata is less compelling. The free tier is limited to 60 pages per month, and the English-only interface is restrictive for international users. Page-based pricing means costs increase with document length rather than question count. But for teams needing collaborative document AI, Humata fills a niche that other tools do not.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1689:  "altsChatpdf.alt4Desc2": "The unique AI-generated audio podcast feature creates natural-sounding conversational summaries of your sources, which is a genuinely novel way to consume research. The tradeoff is Google lock-in: you need a Google account, your data is on Google servers, and the English-focused interface limits international use. NotebookLM also does not support DOCX, PPTX, or XLSX natively.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1697:  "altsChatpdf.alt6Desc2": "ChatDOC offers page-level citations that show the relevant section of the document. The interface is available in English and Chinese. Free users get 2 documents per day with 20 questions each. The Pro plan starts at $5.99 per month. For documents where table accuracy is critical, ChatDOC is worth evaluating, though DocTalk XLSX support may serve similar needs for spreadsheet-heavy workflows.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1714:  "altsChatpdf.faq1Answer": "Google NotebookLM is the best completely free alternative, offering multi-source notebooks and audio podcast generation with no usage limits (Google account required). DocTalk also offers a free demo with no signup required and a free tier with 300 credits per month.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1718:  "altsChatpdf.faq3Answer": "DocTalk has the most advanced citation system with real-time visual highlighting. Click any citation to instantly scroll to and highlight the exact source passage in your document. Other tools only provide page number references.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1738:  "altsNotebooklm.heroDescription": "Google NotebookLM is a powerful free tool for multi-source research, but it requires a Google account, does not support common business formats like DOCX and XLSX, and lacks real-time citation highlighting. Whether you need vendor independence, broader format support, better citation verification, or a multilingual interface, these six alternatives offer compelling reasons to look beyond NotebookLM.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1739:  "altsNotebooklm.metaDescription": "Google NotebookLM is a powerful free tool for multi-source research, but it requires a Google account, does not support common business formats like DOCX and XLSX, and lacks real-time citation highlighting. Whether you need vendor independence, broader format support, better citation verification, or a multilingual interface, these six alternatives offer compelling reasons to look beyond NotebookLM.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1745:  "altsNotebooklm.alt1Desc3Pre": "The free demo requires no signup and no Google account. Paid plans start at $9.99 per month. See our",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1751:  "altsNotebooklm.adv4": "No Google account required",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1755:  "altsNotebooklm.alt2Desc1": "ChatPDF is the most straightforward NotebookLM alternative. Upload a PDF, ask questions, get answers with page references. There is no multi-source notebook concept and no audio podcasts, but for users who just need to query individual PDF files, ChatPDF simplicity is its appeal. The tool has a large established user base and a proven track record.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1764:  "altsNotebooklm.alt4Desc2": "The Team plan costs $49/user/month, making it the most expensive option on this list. Individual plans start at $4.99/month (Student, 100 pages). The interface is English-only. If you need collaborative document AI for a team, Humata is the clear winner. For individual use, other alternatives offer better value.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1772:  "altsNotebooklm.alt6Desc2": "Where NotebookLM creates notebooks from documents you provide, Elicit helps you discover papers you might not have found otherwise. The structured extraction feature automatically pulls key data from papers into a spreadsheet-like view. Elicit offers a free tier with limited usage and a Pro plan for heavy users. It is a complementary tool to document Q&A platforms rather than a direct replacement, ideal for the discovery and organization phases of research.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1786:  "altsNotebooklm.faq2Answer": "DocTalk offers a free demo with no signup required and a free tier with 300 credits per month. ChatPDF offers 2 free PDFs per day. However, no other tool matches NotebookLM fully free unlimited usage, since it is subsidized by Google.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1788:  "altsNotebooklm.faq3Answer": "DocTalk has the most advanced citation system with real-time visual highlighting. Click any citation to scroll to and highlight the exact source passage. Other tools provide page references but not visual highlighting.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1799:  "altsNotebooklm.ctaDescription": "No Google account needed. Upload a document and experience citation highlighting instantly.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1806:  "altsHumata.heroDescription": "Humata has built a solid AI document analysis tool with unique team features and video support, but its page-based pricing, English-only interface, and lack of citation highlighting leave room for improvement. Whether you need better citations, more document formats, multilingual support, or simply better value for individual use, these five alternatives are worth considering.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1807:  "altsHumata.metaDescription": "Humata has built a solid AI document analysis tool with unique team features and video support, but its page-based pricing, English-only interface, and lack of citation highlighting leave room for improvement. Whether you need better citations, more document formats, multilingual support, or simply better value for individual use, these five alternatives are worth considering.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1811:  "altsHumata.alt1Desc1": "DocTalk addresses Humata two biggest gaps: citation verification and language support. Where Humata provides page number references in answers, DocTalk offers real-time citation highlighting. Click any citation in an AI answer to instantly scroll to and highlight the exact source passage in a side-by-side document viewer. This visual verification eliminates the need to manually search for sources.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1813:  "altsHumata.alt1Desc3Pre": "Pricing is also more favorable for individuals. DocTalk Plus at $9.99 per month with 3,000 credits provides more value than Humata Expert at $14.99 per month with 500 pages. The credit model is also more predictable than page-based pricing, since costs depend on question count rather than document length. A free demo requires no signup. See our",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1816:  "altsHumata.adv1": "Real-time citation highlighting (Humata: page references only)",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1819:  "altsHumata.adv4": "Credit-based pricing, more predictable than page-based",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1831:  "altsHumata.alt4Desc1": "Google NotebookLM is the best free Humata alternative. Where Humata free tier limits you to 60 pages per month, NotebookLM is entirely free (with a Google account). The multi-source notebook approach lets you combine PDFs, Google Docs, web URLs, and YouTube transcripts. The AI-generated audio podcast feature creates conversational summaries of your sources.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1832:  "altsHumata.alt4Desc2": "The tradeoff is Google lock-in and format limitations. NotebookLM does not support DOCX, PPTX, or XLSX natively. The interface is primarily English. You need a Google account, and your data is on Google servers. But for budget-conscious users who are comfortable with Google, NotebookLM is hard to beat on value.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1849:  "altsHumata.faq1Answer": "DocTalk is the best Humata alternative for individual users. It offers citation highlighting, 7 document formats, 11 interface languages, and better value pricing ($9.99/month for 3,000 credits vs Humata Expert at $14.99/month for 500 pages).",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1851:  "altsHumata.faq2Answer": "Google NotebookLM is completely free with a Google account. DocTalk offers a free demo with no signup required and a free tier with 300 credits per month. ChatPDF offers 2 free PDFs per day.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1886:  "compareHumata.featureFreeTierCompetitor": "60 pages/mo",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1892:  "compareHumata.featureStartingPriceCompetitor": "$4.99/mo (100 pages)",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1897:  "compareHumata.whatIsHumataDescription": "Humata is an AI document analysis platform launched in 2023 that has expanded from PDF analysis into a broader content tool. It supports PDF and Word documents, and notably also supports video file analysis. Humata offers a free tier with 60 pages per month, a Student plan at $4.99/month (100 pages), an Expert plan at $14.99/month (500 pages), and a Team plan at $49/user/month with collaboration features. The team collaboration functionality, including shared workspaces and role management, sets it apart from individual-focused tools. Humata positions itself as a tool for students, researchers, and professional teams working with dense documents.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1901:  "compareHumata.documentFormatDocTalk": "DocTalk supports seven formats: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, TXT, Markdown, and web URLs. Each format has a dedicated parser that preserves structure. The XLSX parser maintains spreadsheet cell relationships, the PPTX parser preserves slide order and speaker notes, and the URL ingester extracts clean article content from web pages. While DocTalk does not support video, it covers the broadest range of common document formats. See",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1904:  "compareHumata.citationsCompetitor": "Humata provides page number references in its answers. The AI generates competent responses for most document types, with a clean interface for viewing answers. The focus on team collaboration means that answers can be shared and discussed within a workspace.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1909:  "compareHumata.languageSupportDocTalk": "DocTalk offers a fully localized interface in 11 languages. This includes English, Chinese, Spanish, Japanese, German, French, Korean, Portuguese, Italian, Arabic, and Hindi. Every element from navigation to error messages to billing pages is translated. The AI also responds in the language of your question. See",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1912:  "compareHumata.pricingCompetitor": "Humata offers a free tier with 60 pages per month. Paid plans include Student ($4.99/month, 100 pages), Expert ($14.99/month, 500 pages), and Team ($49/user/month, unlimited pages with collaboration). The page-based pricing means costs scale with document length, which can be unpredictable for users working with long documents.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1915:  "compareHumata.pricingDocTalkPart2": "Plus ($9.99/month) includes 3,000 credits with unrestricted Pro mode and export. Pro ($19.99/month) includes 9,000 credits with custom instructions. Credits are consumed per question based on the AI mode used, not per document page. View",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1922:  "compareHumata.securityDocTalk": "DocTalk implements AES-256 encryption for all uploaded documents, SSRF protection for URL ingestion, magic-byte file validation, and GDPR compliance with data export. Documents are never used for AI training. The application runs in non-root Docker containers and uses structured security event logging for audit trails.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1925:  "compareHumata.whoDocTalk2": "People who work with PowerPoint, Excel, or web pages in addition to PDFs",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1927:  "compareHumata.whoDocTalk4": "Budget-conscious users who want more features per dollar ($9.99 for 3,000 credits vs $14.99 for 500 pages)",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1935:  "compareHumata.verdictParagraph1": "Humata has carved out a niche with team collaboration features and video support. For organizations that need shared document analysis with role management, the Team plan provides genuine value. The Student plan at $4.99/month is one of the cheapest entry points in this category, though the 100-page limit is restrictive.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1936:  "compareHumata.verdictParagraph2": "DocTalk offers superior citation highlighting, broader format support (seven formats vs three), 11-language localization, and better value for individual users. The credit-based pricing is more predictable than page-based pricing, and the no-signup demo makes it the easiest to try.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1942:  "compareHumata.faq1Answer": "Yes. DocTalk Plus costs $9.99/month with 3,000 credits, while Humata Student costs $4.99/month with only 100 pages/month, and Humata Expert costs $14.99/month. For most users, DocTalk provides better value per dollar with more generous usage limits and citation highlighting included at every tier.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1944:  "compareHumata.faq2Answer": "Humata provides page references in its answers but does not offer real-time inline citation highlighting. DocTalk lets you click any citation to instantly scroll to and highlight the exact passage in your document viewer.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1991:  "comparePdfai.whatIsPdfaiDescription": "PDF.ai is a web-based tool that lets users upload PDF files and ask questions about their content using AI. Launched during the initial wave of AI document tools in 2023, PDF.ai offers a clean, simple interface focused exclusively on PDF interaction. The tool provides basic question-answering with page number references. PDF.ai attracted early users with its memorable domain name and simple approach. However, development has slowed compared to competitors, and the feature set has not expanded significantly. The tool remains functional for basic PDF Q&A but lacks the advanced features found in newer alternatives.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1994:  "comparePdfai.documentFormatCompetitor": "PDF.ai supports only PDF files, as its name suggests. There is no support for Word documents, spreadsheets, presentations, or web pages. If you need to analyze a non-PDF document, you must convert it to PDF first, which adds friction and can introduce formatting errors.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1998:  "comparePdfai.citationsCompetitor": "PDF.ai provides basic Q&A with page number references. The answers are generally competent for straightforward questions. However, the citation system is limited to page numbers without any visual highlighting or precise source identification.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2015:  "comparePdfai.securityDocTalk": "DocTalk implements comprehensive security: AES-256 encryption for all uploaded documents, SSRF protection for URL ingestion, magic-byte file validation, GDPR data export, cookie consent management, non-root Docker deployment, and structured security logging. Documents are never used for AI training.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2038:  "comparePdfai.faq3Answer": "DocTalk has significantly better citation support with real-time visual highlighting. When you click a citation, the document viewer scrolls to and highlights the exact source passage. PDF.ai provides basic page references without inline highlighting.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2086:  "compareAskyourpdf.citationsCompetitor": "AskYourPDF references page numbers and can extract citations for academic papers, which is particularly useful for researchers building bibliographies. The tool provides competent answers for most document types, with particular strength in academic content.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2091:  "compareAskyourpdf.languageSupportDocTalk": "DocTalk offers a fully translated interface in 11 languages, covering approximately 4.5 billion native speakers worldwide. Every part of the application, from error messages to billing pages, is available in English, Chinese, Spanish, Japanese, German, French, Korean, Portuguese, Italian, Arabic, and Hindi.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2093:  "compareAskyourpdf.pricingCompetitor": "AskYourPDF offers a limited free tier and a Premium plan starting at $14.99 per month that includes the Chrome extension, unlimited documents, and priority processing. An Enterprise plan is available for teams. The API usage is charged separately based on volume.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2106:  "compareAskyourpdf.whoDocTalk2": "People who work with multiple document formats (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, web pages)",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2127:  "compareAskyourpdf.faq2Answer": "AskYourPDF provides page references in its answers, similar to ChatPDF. However, it does not offer the real-time inline citation highlighting that DocTalk provides, where clicking a citation scrolls to and visually highlights the exact passage in your document.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2139:  "compareAskyourpdf.ctaDescription": "See how citation highlighting compares to page references. Upload a document and try it now.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2146:  "useCasesStudents.hero.subtitle": "Upload research papers, textbooks, or dissertations and get AI-powered answers with page-level citations you can verify. Spend less time reading and more time understanding.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2147:  "useCasesStudents.metaDescription": "Upload research papers, textbooks, or dissertations and get AI-powered answers with page-level citations you can verify. Spend less time reading and more time understanding.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2150:  "useCasesStudents.challenge.p1": "Academic research demands an enormous volume of reading. A typical PhD student reads over 100 papers per year, and that number climbs sharply during literature review phases. Each paper averages 20 to 50 pages of dense, technical prose. Manually reviewing a single paper takes one to three hours, depending on the subject complexity and your familiarity with the field.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2156:  "useCasesStudents.helps.summarize.description": "Upload a 50-page paper and ask \"What are the key findings?\" DocTalk returns a structured summary with numbered citations pointing to the exact paragraphs where each finding is stated. What used to take an hour takes seconds.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2164:  "useCasesStudents.helps.quotes.description": "Need to cite a specific passage in your thesis? Ask DocTalk to locate it. \"Where does the author discuss limitations of the study?\" The AI pinpoints the passage and gives you the page number for your citation.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2176:  "useCasesStudents.docTypes.url.detail": "Paste a link to any publicly accessible paper, preprint, or academic web page. DocTalk fetches and processes the content automatically.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2179:  "useCasesStudents.realWorld.thesis.p1": "A graduate student uploads their advisor's recommended reading, a 50-page thesis on machine learning interpretability. Instead of reading end to end, they ask: \"What are the main conclusions of this thesis?\" DocTalk returns a four-point summary, each point linked to a numbered citation. Clicking citation [1] scrolls to page 42 where the author states their primary finding. Clicking [3] jumps to page 47 where the author discusses implications. The student grasps the thesis's core argument in two minutes.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2180:  "useCasesStudents.realWorld.thesis.p2": "Follow-up questions drill deeper: \"What datasets were used in the experiments?\" reveals the exact section describing the experimental setup. \"What limitations does the author acknowledge?\" surfaces the limitations discussion from the final chapter. Each answer is traceable to a specific page.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2182:  "useCasesStudents.realWorld.litReview.p1": "A doctoral candidate working on a literature review about natural language processing in healthcare uploads ten papers sequentially. For each paper, they ask: \"What are the main findings?\" and \"What methodology was used?\" They compile the cited answers into a structured comparison matrix, with each finding traceable to its source paper and page number.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2183:  "useCasesStudents.realWorld.litReview.p2": "This workflow replaces the traditional approach of reading each paper cover to cover, taking handwritten notes, and manually organizing findings. The citations make it trivial to go back and verify any point during the writing process. When the advisor asks \"where did you find that claim about BERT performance,\" the student can point to the exact page in the exact paper.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2189:  "useCasesStudents.realWorld.examPrep.p2": "Every answer includes citations that point back to the textbook pages. When the student encounters a concept they do not fully understand, they click the citation to read the original textbook explanation. This creates an active learning loop that is far more effective than passive re-reading.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2220:  "useCasesStudents.faq.a5": "Yes. DocTalk supports URL ingestion, so you can paste a link to any publicly accessible paper or web page. DocTalk will fetch the content, extract the text, and let you chat with it just like an uploaded file.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2222:  "useCasesStudents.cta.description": "Try DocTalk's free demo with sample documents. See how AI-powered citation highlighting works on real papers. No account required.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2240:  "useCasesHr.helps.policyQA.description": "\"What is the remote work policy?\" or \"How do sick days accumulate?\" Upload your employee handbook and get instant answers with citations pointing to the exact section. No more flipping through 100-page handbooks.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2244:  "useCasesHr.helps.handbook.description": "Upload the entire company handbook and use DocTalk as an intelligent search tool. Ask about any policy, procedure, or guideline and get answers that cite the specific section and page.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2254:  "useCasesHr.docTypes.pdf.detail": "Employee handbooks, policy manuals, and code of conduct documents. Navigate hundreds of pages with AI-assisted search and get cited answers.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2261:  "useCasesHr.realWorld.pto.description": "An HR generalist receives an employee question about PTO accrual after a recent policy update. Instead of searching through the 120-page employee handbook manually, they upload it to DocTalk and ask: \"How many PTO days does an employee accrue after 3 years of service?\" DocTalk returns the answer with a citation pointing to Section 7.2 on page 43, the exact PTO accrual table. The HR generalist can verify the answer against the source and respond to the employee with confidence, citing the specific handbook section.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2269:  "useCasesHr.realWorld.onboarding.description": "A new employee starting at a company receives a stack of onboarding documents: the employee handbook, benefits enrollment guide, IT security policy, and code of conduct. Instead of reading hundreds of pages in their first week, they upload each document and ask practical questions: \"When is the deadline to enroll in health insurance?\" \"What is the dress code policy?\" \"How do I request time off?\" Each answer comes with a citation, so the employee can read the full policy context when needed while getting quick answers for immediate questions.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2290:  "useCasesHr.cta.description": "Try DocTalk's free demo with sample documents. See how AI-powered citation highlighting works. No account required.",

Did not run git. I ran `node --test frontend/tests/attribution.test.cjs`; it passes.

1. **PARTIAL**: `landing_path` now redacts dynamic IDs/tokens via `safeLandingPath()` and is used in `readAttribution()` at [attribution.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:113). But the same public events still send raw `path: window.location.pathname` at [analytics.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/analytics.ts:14), and backend stores it in `metadata_json` at [events.py](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/backend/app/api/events.py:118). From `/d/<documentId>`, unauth users can open auth at [DocumentReaderPageClient.tsx](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/d/[documentId]/DocumentReaderPageClient.tsx:305), so the document ID can still be stored.

2. **FIXED**: “No identifiers” is corrected to “no device identifier” plus signed-in account linkage. Code still links signed-in events through proxy auth and `user_id`, matching the copy: [route.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts:106), [events.py](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/backend/app/api/events.py:120).

3. **PARTIAL**: original demo/page-kind/date disclosure is fixed: [PrivacyPageClient.tsx](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/app/privacy/PrivacyPageClient.tsx:27), [en.json](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:220). All 11 locale keys are updated consistently. But the copy says “which kind of page,” while raw `path` still records exact current path, so privacy accuracy remains partial.

4. **FIXED**: UTM values are now slug-like, length-bounded, lowercased, and drop email/phone-ish/UUID/path-query shapes: [attribution.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:101).

5. **FIXED**: referrer filtering now requires http(s), ignores own DocTalk/Vercel hosts, and expands auth/payment/webmail return hops: [attribution.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:39), [attribution.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:81). No material remaining referrer gap found.

6. **PARTIAL**: tests cover the main new sanitizers and first-touch cache, but miss the residual raw `path` leak and unknown single-segment landing paths. `safeLandingPath('/john-smith')` would be kept as `/john-smith` by the fallback at [attribution.ts](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/.claude/worktrees/website-seo-audit-0bec36/frontend/src/lib/attribution.ts:116); that should probably be `/*` unless the first segment is an explicit known bucket.

**Verdict: SHIP-WITH-FIXES**. Fix the public-event `path` field by sanitizing it with the same route bucketing, and tighten unknown single-segment `safeLandingPath` fallback.
